#### Finding 3 — the staleness caveat is explicit and correctly scoped
The addendum blockquote (l.364) states: "**The audit above is a point-in-time snapshot captured on 2026-10-20. It is not current and must not be read as current.** The counts in §1 Executive Summary, Appendix A and Appendix B were measured on 2026-10-20 and are now stale. They have been left unedited deliberately … The figures below supersede the 2026-10-20 counts **for counting purposes only** — the triage judgments above remain those of 2026-10-20 and have not been re-verified."

This is exactly the required labelling: the 2026-10-20 counts are preserved unchanged, the 2026-10-21 counts are labelled as a dated snapshot, and the addendum does not claim the triage was re-performed. The card's note that "7 open PRs as at 2026-10-21" is acceptable because the date is stated on the figure.

#### Finding 4 — scope discipline
The PR adds one file: `docs/tracking/backlog-audit-2026-10.md`. No code, no contract, no workflow is touched, so no ADR-lint impact is expected.

**Evidence level:** L0 static (byte-identity plus independent live GitHub API re-verification of every recorded count). No code is executed by this PR; it is a tracking document. The live re-query is L0 external-state verification against the GitHub API, not a system test.

**Note (non-blocking):** the addendum's figures will drift again as PRs merge. The addendum is already labelled as a dated snapshot, so no action is required for this PR; a refresh is only warranted if the document is intended to remain the current source of truth, in which case the addendum should be re-dated when refreshed.
